scope: Module 11 selected encoder history horizon, wire-window cap and fallible exact-owner reuse
contracts: Only MAX_HISTORY_BYTES visibility changes in match_search.rs. No other plain-record, hash or leaf implementation change.

encode retains its preflight SearchShape. Ring metadata admits the shared 1 MiB bound without eager payload allocation; only the first nonempty block reserves min(configured history, actual frame window). Empty one-shot window zero creates no ring.
No new unsafe operation or feature. Ring read/write operations compose the existing independently selected unsafe-ring-history implementation; exact retained owners and no_std behavior are preserved.

Tiny horizons 1/2/7/8 and width8 keys cross short and empty block/Flush boundaries under Greedy/Chain/Lazy, with or without a three-byte dictionary. Every retained suffix byte and absolute counter is verified; no missing bytes are padded.

All three named strategies find a >=60000-byte match at distance196608 with that retained horizon and window262144. The witness disappears with history131072 or with a requested1MiB horizon capped by window131072.
A one-byte horizon evicts frame zero but leaves complete dictionary-only matching eligible independently; subsequent frame positions beyond the advertised window remove dictionary eligibility.
Borrowed NonClone owner reservations grow1,2,7,8,131073,1048576 then shrink/regrow without new allocation within high-water capacity; one owner identity persists.

Every one of the six positive ring growth requests is independently failed, leaving caller output, literal state, logical history, retained allocation and frame counter unchanged; reset/retry succeeds while preserving selected options and the exact ring owner.

If output allocation fails after successful history reservation, payload capacity remains reusable but no history/input is committed. Reset recovery reuses the reservation with its allocator failure armed.
Both archived default replays preserve all76 frame fingerprints and capacities. Requested maximum metadata alone does not change default ring allocation sizes or allocation failure schedules.
